note: Hand-labelled resolution verdicts used to measure the judge's agreement with a human reader. Labels are the author's, not an attorney's; the point is that the judge's behaviour is a measured number, not an assumption.

conflict.company_text: Liability capped at fees paid in the preceding 12 months.
conflict.vendor_text: Vendor liability capped at $5,000 in the aggregate.
conflict.conflict_explanation: A $5,000 cap on a six-figure contract removes any meaningful remedy.
conflict.resolution: Replace the $5,000 cap with a mutual cap equal to fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, with carve-outs for indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

conflict.company_text: Governed by the laws of New York.
conflict.vendor_text: Governed by the laws of California.
conflict.resolution: Adopt Delaware law with venue in Wilmington, or alternatively keep New York, or alternatively accept California with arbitration in London; the parties may choose whichever they prefer at the time of dispute.

conflict.company_text: Either party may terminate for convenience on 60 days' notice.
conflict.vendor_text: Vendor may terminate for convenience on 10 days' notice; Customer may not terminate for convenience.
conflict.conflict_explanation: One-way convenience termination on very short notice.
conflict.resolution: Delete the vendor's termination rights entirely; only Customer may terminate, at any time, without notice or refund obligations.

conflict.company_text: Net 45 from receipt of a correct invoice.
conflict.vendor_text: Net 15; 2% per month late fee; suspension after 5 days.
conflict.conflict_explanation: Materially shorter payment window with punitive late fees.
conflict.resolution: Net 30 from receipt of a correct invoice; disputed amounts withheld in good faith without penalty; late interest at 1% per month after a 15-day grace period; no suspension without 30 days' written notice of non-payment.

conflict.conflict_explanation: Survival period far shorter than standard.
conflict.resolution: Extend the survival period to a reasonable time.

conflict.conflict_explanation: Long lock-in with an early notice window.
conflict.resolution: Accept automatic renewal for 12-month terms with a 60-day non-renewal window and a vendor reminder 90 days before expiry.

conflict.company_text: Vendor indemnifies for third-party IP claims.
conflict.vendor_text: Customer indemnifies Vendor for all claims of any kind.
conflict.resolution: Both parties indemnify each other for everything, uncapped, including each other's own negligence, so that neither party bears any risk.

conflict.company_text: No assignment without consent, except to a successor in a merger.
conflict.vendor_text: Vendor may assign freely; Customer needs consent.
conflict.resolution: Make the assignment clause mutual: neither party may assign without the other's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except to an affiliate or successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, with written notice.

conflict.conflict_explanation: Coverage below standard given data access.
conflict.resolution: Vendor to carry insurance appropriate to the engagement.

conflict.conflict_explanation: Five-day difference in the change-notice window.
conflict.resolution: Accept the vendor's 35-day notice period for scope changes; the difference has no operational impact and conforming to one number avoids ambiguity.

conflict.vendor_text: Vendor owns all deliverables; Customer receives a term-limited licence.
conflict.conflict_explanation: Ownership of bespoke work product reversed.
conflict.resolution: Customer owns the deliverables during the term and Vendor owns them after termination, with each party free to sublicense the other's rights to third parties.

conflict.company_text: Executive escalation, then courts; injunctive relief available.
conflict.vendor_text: Binding arbitration in Vendor's home city; class-action waiver.
conflict.conflict_explanation: Mandatory arbitration in a distant forum.
conflict.resolution: Replace mandatory arbitration with a 30-day executive escalation followed by mediation; if unresolved, litigation in the agreed venue, with either party retaining the right to seek injunctive relief for IP or confidentiality breaches.
